subject: QuietBridge reserved-island synthesis + next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@quietbridge.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@quietbridge.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuietBridge reserved-island synthesis + next steps

Hi Elena / Amit —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps for procurement and ops. If I missed something, flag it and we’ll update.

High-level pain / goals we heard
- Peak inference latency spikes during live scoring windows (9–11am PT) causing user-facing timeouts on interactive features.
- Cost is being driven by current multi-tenant bursts — QuietBridge wants predictable unit economics for production.
- Regulatory need for dataset isolation on a per-product basis (PHI-adjacent telemetry) and audit logs for every model invocation.

Proposed Redwood fit (what we discussed)
- Reserved "island" (dedicated GPU pool) sized for sustained throughput of ~1200 tokens/sec with 3x burst headroom for traffic bursts — maps to 4 A100-equivalent cards initially, autoscale to 8 for seasonal spikes.
- Tenant isolation via physical pool assignment + VPC peering; optional HSM/KMS integration for key management.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool; latency p95 target at call-level ~220ms for the standard chat model (configured quantized variant).

Open questions we promised to answer
1) Exact inference footprint per request (avg tokens per call) — you said ~350 tokens average active sessions, confirmation requested.
2) SOC2 + penetration test evidence requests — Marissa will follow up with a package.
3) Procurement cadence / PO timeline — Amit, you mentioned an internal review next week. Any target date?

Attachments I’m sharing now
- quietbridge-mop-draft.pdf (operational runbook outline: rollout, canary, fallback to hosted)
- slo-table-quietbridge.xlsx (initial SLA/kpi table to map to your SRE metrics)

Next steps (owner, ETA)
- Connor: update MOP with pricing bands and commit-day assumptions — EOD Wed (6/23).
- Marissa: send SOC2 & pentest artifacts + recommended security checklist — Tue (6/22).
- Amit / Elena: confirm avg tokens per request and procurement window — please reply with dates.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on priorities today.

Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs:
- quietbridge-mop-draft.pdf (PDF, 450KB)
- slo-table-quietbridge.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuietBridge reserved-island synthesis + next steps

Connor / team —

Thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Average tokens per interactive scoring call: 320–360 (we’re comfortable using 350 as a working average).
- Peak concurrent requests during the 9–11am window: ~180–220 concurrent sessions.
- Procurement: our IT procurement lead is aiming to have a signed PO by 7/02; pending budget committee sign-off on 6/28.

On security: please prioritize the SOC2 and pentest artifacts. We’ll need to map log retention options to 13 months for audit. Also want to confirm whether the dedicated island can enforce customer-side firewall rules (we use a strict inbound allowlist today).

Appreciate Marissa’s help.

—Elena
CTO | QuietBridge AI

On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Elena / Amit —
>
> I’ll send the SOC2 plus the most recent pen test summary and our standard security checklist within the hour. For log retention we support 13/25/36 month tiers; I’ll note the 13-month requirement.
>
> Regarding firewall: yes — dedicated islands can be deployed behind a customer-managed firewall with a strict allowlist. We’ll add a short section to the MOP with the exact network flow and required CIDRs.
>
> Marissa

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuietBridge reserved-island synthesis + next steps

Elena — perfect, thanks for confirming the token avg and procurement window. Quick updates: 

1) MOP & pricing: attached updated MOP includes two pricing bands — the initial reserved island (4x A100 equiv) and an autoscale path to 8x with burst pricing. I also included the network/CIDR snippet Marissa mentioned.
2) SLA table: p95 latency 220ms (quantized model), availability 99.9% on the dedicated pool. We’ve included an RTO for failover to hosted fallback (best-effort) in the runbook.
3) Ops checklist: canary rollout plan for first 2 weeks (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) and rollback criteria (error spike >3% or latency increase >40% over baseline).

Please see attached: quietbridge-mop-draft.pdf (v2) and slo-table-quietbridge.xlsx (updated with your 350 token avg).

Action items recap
- Connor: finalize pricing sheet and send commercial proposal along with redlines template — Fri (6/25) EOD.
- Marissa: upload SOC2/pentest to secure drive and share access to QuietBridge security team — Wed (6/23) morning.
- Elena / Amit: confirm procurement sign-off date and any legal must-haves (e.g., data residency clause) — target 6/28 reply.

If that looks right I’ll convert the proposal into a commercial term sheet and route to my AE for a pricing signature request.

Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Connor / team —

All looks good from our side. Procurement target is still 7/02 but we’ll aim for 6/28 as the date to lock commercial terms. Two small asks before we sign: 
1) Can we get explicit language around data residency in the term sheet (US-only hosting and audit copies)?
2) Can Redwood provide a test harness or small pilot (2-day smoke test) as part of the onboarding to validate latency under our load profile?

If you can include those in the commercial term sheet we’ll expedite internal approvals.

Thanks — Amit
Head of Platform | QuietBridge AI
